points.description: States that an unlimited number of constructors can be created for a class — accept 'unlimited', 'any number', 'as many as needed/wanted', or any wording meaning there is no fixed upper limit. An answer that says only 'more than one', 'multiple', 'several' or 'many' without conveying that there is no limit earns part marks.
points.partial_credit: Half marks for saying more than one/multiple/many but not conveying that the number is unlimited.

levels.says: Says a class can have more than one constructor (multiple, several, many) but does not state or imply that the number is unlimited.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the idea that the number of constructors is unlimited (any number, no fixed limit). An answer saying only 'more than one' or 'many' earns half marks because it is vague about there being no upper limit. Answers giving a fixed number (e.g. one, two) earn no marks.
